page: Microsoft Azure D372ds_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by Intel processors within the Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization environment. The configuration features 372 dedicated virtual cores paired with 1488 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor. The instance does not include GPU acceleration.

Storage capabilities are defined by 22680 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, providing low-latency ephemeral disk access alongside Premium Storage support for external persistent disk volumes. Dedicated resource allocation ensures predictable multi-threaded throughput across all 372 vCPUs without contention from neighboring workloads. The substantial local storage footprint minimizes reliance on external network-attached volumes for temporary data handling, improving qualitative efficiency for heavy I/O pipelines.

The combination of extensive core density, substantial memory capacity, and high-capacity local NVMe storage makes Microsoft Azure D372ds_v7 well aligned with distributed data processing, enterprise relational and non-relational database clusters, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency software build environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D372ds_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 372 dedicated Intel vCPUs and 1488 GB of system memory. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance maintains a consistent 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio offering 4.0 GB of RAM per core without discrete GPU acceleration. A primary hardware characteristic is its 22680 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage, designed for high-throughput, low-latency ephemeral read and write operations alongside Premium Storage support. Dedicated core provisioning prevents hypervisor resource sharing, ensuring consistent compute and memory availability across the entire core topology. With its high vCPU scale and multi-terabyte local disk capacity, D372ds_v7 accommodates compute-intensive batch processing, enterprise-scale relational and NoSQL databases, extensive distributed analytics nodes, in-memory caches requiring fast local spillover storage, and parallel compilation workloads.
